head: claude/subsession-registry-coupling-handoff-check
title: sub-session registry: couple the spawn to the record, and a handoff-readiness check
body:
## Summary

`docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json` is the only thing a manager arriving **cold** can read to pick up its predecessor's sub-sessions; a session it does not name is, to that successor, a session that does not exist. `MI-15-SESSIONS-REGISTRY-INCOMPLETE` recorded **3 of 6** absent on 2026-09-01 and applied the remedy *"remember to register."* On 2026-09-02 it was **6 of 9, five of them LIVE**, while that row still sat at `landed_unproven`. **Remember-to has now failed twice**, so this ships machinery instead: a spawn path that goes *through* the registry, two detectors with deliberately different reach, and a handoff-readiness verdict.

### ⚠️ It is worse than briefed — re-measured, with the population stated

**Population:** all **60** sessions returned by `list_sessions(mine=true, limit=60)` at ~2026-09-02T06:30Z, graded against the **30** registry rows at `main` `550c9f6d`. 1 excluded as the manager itself, 4 excluded as `ARCHIVED` (cannot be orphaned) → **55 graded**.

- **26 of 55 graded sessions appear nowhere in the registry.**
- **17 of those 26 carry the manager's own id as `parent_session_id`** — sessions it demonstrably spawned. (The other 9 record no parent; unattributable, so kept — the fail-safe direction for an alarm about losing work is to alarm.)
- **5 of the 26 were `RUNNING`** at the time of the read.

## Deliverable 1 — spawning and registering

### ⚠️ True coupling is impossible here, and this says so rather than faking it

**The repo does not own the spawn.** A sub-session is created by the `create_session` MCP tool; nothing in this repository sits on that call path — no hook, no wrapper, no interposition point — so no code here can make the registry write happen *as part of* the spawn. A mechanism claiming otherwise would look like a coupling and not be one.

What ships instead, in descending strength:

**(a) The registry is on the path to the thing the manager actually wants.** `session_registry.py register` writes the row **and prints the spawn prompt**. A sub-session cannot run correctly without a prompt, so the cheapest correct route now goes *through* the registry rather than around it. Still bypassable by hand-writing a prompt — **necessary, not sufficient**, which is why (b) and (c) exist. `.claude/skills/delegate-work/SKILL.md` now says generate the prompt, not hand-write it.

**(b) An OFFLINE detector that runs in CI on every PR.** The manager already writes a session id into `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json::items[].owner` when it assigns work — a **second, independent** record of the same fact, written at a different moment for a different reason. An owner id absent from the registry is a lost session, found from **two file reads**: no MCP, no network, no live state. ⚠️ **Partial by construction and stated as such:** a session in neither file is invisible to it too. It catches the *overlap* of two incomplete records, which is strictly more than the zero either caught alone.

**(c) A LIVE detector the manager runs.** Only a session holding `list_sessions` can enumerate what is running, and **CI holds no MCP tools**. So it cannot be scheduled; what forces it is deliverable 2 refusing to grade `ready` without it.

### What makes (b) run, and proof it fires in both directions

New guard `session-registry-guard` in `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`, `when: None` (every PR — the registry is written by whichever session spawns next, so a check that only runs when someone touches the work store is not a check).

| | Planted | Result | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control | clean tree | quiet | **0** |
| **A** | unregistered owner on an `in_flight` item | `owner_unregistered`, names the id | **1** |
| **B** | *same* owner on a `done` item | **quiet** — censused, not enforced | **0** |
| **C** | duplicate `session_id` in the registry | `structural=malformed`, names the row | **1** |

**B is the one that proves it discriminates**: it refuses the *absence on an enforced state*, not merely the presence of an unknown id.

**Not a wall — verified before wiring.** `status --strict` exits **0** at this head. Enforcement is scoped to `in_flight` (where losing a session costs live work); the **3** owners still absent on `landed_unproven` items are **censused and printed on every run**, so the narrow enforcement cannot hide the wider number.

## Deliverable 2 — `scripts/ops/handoff_check.py`

The lease is deliberately **not** a handoff — its own docstring says takeover is TIME-BASED *because a session that dies cannot hand over*. Right for a manager that **died**; a manager stepping down deliberately is the other case, and everything the successor inherits was until now "remember to." **The lease is not touched.**

Five checks, each of which can genuinely fail, each mapping to something a successor loses. Nothing included that cannot fail:

1. `live_registry` — an observed live sub-session absent from the registry
2. `checklist_owners` — a checklist owner on an `in_flight` item absent from it
3. `lease` — you must actually **hold** the lease to hand it over
4. `manager_state_pushed` — registry/checklist/lease edits that never reached `origin` (the lease already states this rule *for itself*; it is exactly as true of the registry, which a successor opens **first**)
5. `pending_spawns` — a `spawn_pending` row whose id was never confirmed

**Three states, never collapsed:** `ready` / `not_ready` / **`unknown` (we could not look)**. Exit codes **0 / 3 / 4** keep all three apart, so a caller cannot treat "we could not look" as a pass. FAIL dominates UNKNOWN (a known blocker is a definite not-ready); UNKNOWN dominates PASS.

⚠️ **`ready` is UNOBTAINABLE without a live observation, and that is the enforcement rather than an inconvenience.** There is deliberately **no flag that asserts the registry is fine** — *asserting it is what failed twice.*

**Live run at this head** (`readiness=not_ready`, exit 3) named the real blocker: two `in_flight` owners absent from the registry, while lease / pushed-state / pending-spawns passed.

### ⚠️ Not registered with `collapsed-state-guard`, deliberately

The guard requires a consumer **outside** the producer module. `readiness` is consumed by `handoff_check.py`'s own `_EXIT` and `_ADVICE` tables (both name all three) plus its tests. Registering it would make its **own test** the sole external consumer — satisfying the guard without adding a real branch, which is the *"cheaper to lie to than to satisfy"* shape the guard's own header warns about. It becomes registrable the moment a real external caller branches on it.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — manager-coordination machinery only. No data schema, no model boundary, no pipeline stage, no deployment stage, no public API, no config shape. Does not touch the order path, `config/`, or any live-trading file.

## Test plan

- [x] `session_registry.py --self-test` — **25/25 PASS**
- [x] `handoff_check.py --self-test` — **21/21 PASS**
- [x] `tests/test_session_registry.py` + `tests/test_handoff_check.py` — **47 cases pass**. ⚠️ **`pytest` is absent in this container**, so these were run through a stdlib shim implementing `mark.parametrize` / `raises` / `tmp_path`. Real `pytest` runs in CI; I am **not** reporting them green on this container's authority.
- [x] Guard fires on planted defects **and stays quiet when clean** — the 4-row table above
- [x] `status --strict` exits 0 at this head (not a wall)
- [x] `ruff check .` — clean **tree-wide** (it caught two `E741`s of mine; fixed in `0bbdee8`)
- [x] `SESSIONS.json` diff verified a clean append: **27 insertions, 1 deletion** (the `updated_at` line) — no whole-file reformat, and a test pins the non-ASCII serialisation
- [x] `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **PASS 68 · FAIL 3**. ⚠️ **All 3 are tooling absent from this container, not my diff**, and I checked rather than assumed: `artifact-validity-guard` and `operator-owed-guard` both exit on `No module named pytest` (reproduced directly), `layer-guard` exits **127** (`lint-imports` not found). **I could not run those three** — CI can.
- [ ] CI green

## ⚠️ Scope changes and findings the manager must read

**1. I wrote `SESSIONS.json` after saying I would not.** My board `START` claimed I would only read the three manager-owned files. I appended **two rows**, because the guard cannot be a *failing* CI check while the tree already violates it, and I will not ship a report-only detector — that is the failure one level up. Both rows are **reconstructed, and say so in their own text**: every field comes from `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json` plus **one `get_session` poll**, nothing inferred. It is a trailing-array append — the most mergeable shape available on a hot file.

**2. `session_01PnQLKnuezWVB4D47PtnTqR` is LIVE and was unregistered.** Polled, not assumed: `SESSION_STATUS_IDLE`, `status_bucket BLOCKED`, parent = the manager, branch `claude/phase-h-decision-roundtrip`, owning **MI-08 — Phase H, the control half**. It carries **three unactioned `needs_action` items**: set `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN` after merge · fire `work-decision-commit` on `workflow_dispatch` · unblock the stalled Streamlit-retirement branch. **IDLE is not dead** — a handoff before this row existed would have dropped live Phase-H work *and* those three requests. Found by the offline detector, by a route entirely independent of the count that motivated this task.

**3. `session_01LqVvgvusnN87neBn5ayzhg` is ARCHIVED/FAILED** (branch `claude/claude-ping-double-delivery-x4mq2p`), matching MI-18's own note. Registered anyway — not to rescue it, but because MI-18 is still `in_flight` and PR #10694 stands, and a successor seeing an `in_flight` item owned by a session it has no record of hits the same dead end one step removed.

**4. Two things my dispatch prompt told me to read do not exist at `main` `550c9f6d`.** There is no `⚠️_registry_completeness` note at the top of `SESSIONS.json` and no `recurrence` block on `MI-15`. I checked both files directly. I did not add them — they are manager-owned state.

**5. My own detector was wrong on its first live run, and the fix is in this PR.** It reported `session_context`, `session_status` and `session_inbound` as unregistered sessions: the MCP result arrives inside an `<other-session>` wrapper, `json.loads` failed on the whole file, and the free-text fallback matched **JSON key names**. **3 of 32 findings were nonexistent.** Fixed by slicing the outermost JSON before parsing and tightening the text-fallback pattern (≥16 chars, must contain a digit). Both have regression tests.

## Filed for follow-ups

- **3 owner ids remain absent** on `landed_unproven` items (`MI-06`, `MI-17`, `MI-20`) — printed by every guard run, deliberately not enforced. The manager should register or dismiss them.
- **The live detector cannot be scheduled.** `list_sessions` is an MCP tool; CI has none. `handoff_check` refusing `ready` without an observation is the strongest forcing function available from inside the repo — if the manager never runs it, nothing catches the live half. Worth an `OPEN-ITEMS.json` row; I did not add one (hot file, and the manager owns it).
- **`MI-15` should move off `landed_unproven`** — its stated remedy has now demonstrably failed twice.
- I did **not** touch `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json` (a live manager is writing it).
